[RFCS.23.7] **Receiving a fact.** An engine asserting a `FactExternal` checks
its `schema_hash` ([RFCS.23.3]), decodes it, asserts it, and resolves each
nested fact-reference, innermost first:

1. a live fact of that schema **equal** to the inlined copy is the same fact,
   and the slot refers to it: nothing is asserted for the copy, and the fact
   keeps its `event_id`. Of several equal live facts, it is the one with the
   lowest `fact_id` ([RFCS.6.9]). With no equal live fact, an earlier inlined
   copy in the same `FactExternal` equal to this one is the same fact, and the
   slot refers to what that copy resolved to;
2. otherwise, if no live fact of that schema has the same identity key, the
   inlined copy is asserted and the slot refers to it;
3. otherwise — a live fact with that key whose values differ — the engine must
   refuse the whole `FactExternal`: nothing is asserted and nothing is replaced.

**Equal** is the no-op reassertion's comparison ([LFAC.2.5.1], [LFAC.2.5.4]),
slot by slot over the inlined copy's slots, and a fact-reference slot is equal
when it resolves to the same fact. Resolving innermost first is what lets an
outer copy compare equal: its references are already resolved to live facts.
On a `logical` schema `ts` is left out, as the no-op test leaves it out
([LFAC.9.1]). On any other schema it is compared like any slot, so a copy that
differs from a live fact only in `ts` is another fact.

**`KIND_NULL` in a fact-reference slot is a reference with no target**
([RFCS.23.4]). The engine must admit it whether or not the slot is nullable, and
resolves and asserts nothing for it. In a nullable slot it is `null`. In any other
fact-reference slot the slot refers to no fact, and a read of it finds the target
gone ([NFCT.2.3]). It is equal to a live fact's slot that is `null` or whose target
has gone, so a live fact holding such a reference is the same fact as its own
copy, and a replay resolves it as the live run did ([RFCS.24.2]).

**A reference is resolved once, before anything is asserted.** Steps 1
to 3 judge every reference on working memory as the call finds it, and the engine
must not judge one again during the delivery. One of the delivery's own asserts
can remove a fact a reference resolved to, whether that fact was live or is an
inlined copy the delivery asserted: an answer's supersede ([LCRS.6.2.4]) retracts
it, or a retraction that supersede cascades into does. That refuses nothing and
stops nothing. The slot refers to that fact, and a read of the slot finds the
target gone ([NFCT.2.3]). No rule runs inside a delivery, so no rule can tell this
from a target that left after it. The engine must do this without reading a
removed fact's storage ([RDSC.9.9]).

Every fact asserted here, the received fact and each inlined copy, gets this
engine's own `event_id`, as any assert does ([LFST.5.6]). The received fact
itself is an ordinary assert: a live fact equal to it makes it a no-op
reassertion ([LFAC.2.5.1]).

**One `FactExternal` is one input**, however many facts receiving it asserts.
The engine must sample its clocks once for it ([LTIM.2.8.4]), and every fact
it asserts, each inlined copy and the received fact, takes that sample as its
assertion time ([RFCS.23.5]).

The entry point and its result codes are the integration's ([NCBK.10]).
